item.title: Odd Kid Club Vol.2___ Emphatic Dance Music <3 — Sat Sep 19, 10:00 PM — TBA
item.description:
/lineup @KushArora aka Only Now digital polyglot Melonwater jujube orkid @murderclub Odd Kid Club returns for Vol. 2 — a night of emphatic dance music for odd kids and kindred spirits, unfolding inside a secret Toronto space. From emotion, through music, back to you. Same warm energy, same open dance floor. Come ready for deep bass, bold sounds, and wherever the night takes us. This time, we welcome Only Now, the live project of Bay Area producer Kush Arora. Having performed at MUTEK and earned recognition from The Wire, FACT, and XLR8R, Kush brings his Indian musical roots into a world of heavy bass and raw electronic sound. Live, the music moves between intimacy and intensity—sometimes meditative, sometimes explosive, always made to be felt together. No fixed genre, no need to fit in. Come curious, move freely, and bring your beautiful weirdness. See you in the room <3 ‍
Source: YOHOMO

item.description: Open World Toronto Film Festival (OWTFF) returns for its 11th edition from September 25 to 27, 2026, for three unforgettable days celebrating art, film, culture and human connection in the heart of Toronto. Discover bold independent films and meet the filmmakers and artists behind them through screenings, red carpet interviews, filmmaker Q&As, industry conversations, networking, live entertainment, awards and special presentations. OWTFF brings together filmmakers, artists, industry professionals and audiences from diverse communities, creating a vibrant space where new voices are discovered, creativity is celebrated and meaningful connections are made. Join us at Kensington Studios in Toronto's iconic Kensington Market neighbourhood and experience independent cinema as it was meant to be experienced: together, on the big screen and surrounded by a community that loves the arts. September 25 to 27, 2026 Kensington Studios, 19 Kensington Avenue, Toronto Official website: http://www.owtf

item.title: Art on A Tuesday/Show Friday's — Fri Oct 23, 6:30 PM — Half Note 416
item.description:
Art on a Tuesday returns to Toronto on Friday, October 23 for an intimate, curated night of live entertainment, art, food and connection.
Taking place at Half Note 416 in Scarborough, the evening brings multiple forms of entertainment together under one roof — live R&B, comedy, magic and mentalism, spoken word, violin, visual art, featured creatives and DJs.
The October 23 lineup includes comedians Sai Kit Lo and Moe Ismail, magician and mentalist Francisco Perez, R&B singer Rose SHIKU, violinist Daniela Olano, spoken word artist Marie-Lauren Gregoire Drummond (MLG), along with featured visual artists and creatives.

item.title: One Last Backcountry Weekend in Frontenac — Sat Oct 24, 6:30 AM
item.description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club **Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/weekend-in-frontenac)**
**Fall (aka shoulder season) camping brings the serene beauty of the backcountry, without the crowds and bugs.**
At this time of year, Frontenac will be less busy and the trail into Big Clear Lake belongs mostly to us. It's a 9km hike to reach the site, working through root tangled trails and stretches of open granite typical of this stretch of the Canadian Shield. Only the most stubborn leaves will remain on the trees and you’ll enjoy long sightlines through bare branches where the canopy used to be. The pace is steady and moderate the whole way in, never technical but never quite letting up either.

item.title: TPL: Laverne Cox: Transcendent in conversation with Kai Cheng Thom — Thu Sep 10, 6:00 PM — Toronto Public Library - North York Central Library
item.description:
[Off-site] Join us at the Toronto Public Library North York Concourse on September 10th for an evening with Laverne Cox! Laverne Cox is a powerhouse in the fight for transgender rights and representation—but her path from a struggling trans actress to a cultural movement was anything but easy.
In Transcendent, Laverne invites us into her journey as a transgender woman in Hollywood; confronting childhood trauma, shame and feelings of unworthiness; and, ultimately, healing.
Laverne Cox speaks with author and activist Kai Cheng Thom about making history for her role in Orange is the New Black, her fearless advocacy for LGBTQ+ rights and finding her voice in a world that can too often feel lonely and unaccepting. Q&A to follow. Books available for purchase. For tickets and more information, check out the Eventbrite page!
